Situation1: It seems your friend is confused about the meeting spot, and you need to send a message right now to confirm it.
Expectation2: Communicate with clients and vendors regarding financial matters.
Situation2: A client has an inquiry about a specific line item on their most recent invoice.
Story: My phone buzzes twice in quick succession. I glance down and see a message from my friend, Sarah: “Hey, are we meeting at the café or the park? Let me know!” At the same moment, an email notification pops up from a client, Mr. Patel, with the subject line: “Invoice #2043 – Urgent Question.” I know Sarah gets anxious when plans are unclear, and I promised her I’d be more communicative after our last misunderstanding. But Mr. Patel is one of our biggest clients, and he’s flagged this as urgent. My manager always stresses the importance of prompt, clear responses to clients, especially about financial details. I can feel my heart rate pick up as I stare at my phone, torn between quickly clarifying things for Sarah and making sure Mr. Patel gets the attention he expects. Both are waiting for me, both expecting me to respond right now. I hesitate, my fingers hovering over the screen, feeling the weight of both roles pressing in on me.
